phase: 6 -- competitor directories as DISCOVERY LEAD SOURCES only
standing_rule: A competitor directory is an AUDIT lane, not an acquisition lane, and it is never policy authority. No competitor policy text is published, quoted into authority, or used to grade a row. Any candidate found here must go back through first-party verification.

attempts.note: refuses a plain client on every lodging path tried
robots.txt names a sitemap index; the index itself is 403
serves one 405 KB client-rendered shell for every path, including /robots.txt and /sitemap_index.xml. A 200 that returns the same shell for a robots file is not a served page.
guessed city path does not exist and robots.txt names no sitemap

free_static_lane.conclusion: the competitor lane is reachable only with an attended browser, which is where this order took it

attended_lane.why_this_one: it is the directory the committed doctrine has already measured, against Indianapolis, so its traps are known and testable here

inert_filter_test.why: the committed doctrine warns that this directory's QUERY-STRING category filter is inert -- ?type=hotels and ?type=rentals return byte-identical results -- and that the real filter is a PATH segment. This order tested the path segment on three values.

observations.headline: There are 135 pet friendly hotels in Cincinnati
There are 36 pet friendly hotels in Cincinnati
There are 99 pet friendly vacation rentals in Cincinnati

inert_filter_test.finding: The PATH filter is live -- three values, three different cohorts. But the UNFILTERED page calls itself 'hotels' while serving hotels and vacation rentals together. Its 135 is a mixed-category number wearing a hotel label. The directory's real Cincinnati hotel inventory is 36.
inert_filter_test.consequence: Taking 135 as the competitor's hotel census would have manufactured a discovery gap out of 99 vacation rentals. This is the committed inert-filter and headline-count traps in their sharpest form, and the arithmetic proves it rather than asserting it.

served_cohort_harvest.why_partial: the listing renders twelve teaser cards and gates the rest behind an interactive date selection; scrolling does not extend it (page height and link count both stay fixed). The full served cohort was NOT harvested and this order does not report one.
served_cohort_harvest.what_is_reported: the twelve rows that did render, reconciled honestly, and the three headline counts, which are the directory's own claims about its own size

category_hygiene.note: both are vacation-rental rows served on a page headed 'pet friendly hotels'. 2 of 12 is consistent with the ~9.5% non-hotel rate the committed doctrine measured elsewhere.

geography_note: BringFido scopes this listing to the literal city string 'Cincinnati, OH'. Atlas's market is the tri-state metro and includes Florence KY, Erlanger KY, Newport KY, Mason OH, West Chester OH, Hamilton OH, Middletown OH, Lawrenceburg IN and more. The directory cannot see most of this market, so its inventory is not comparable to the census without that caveat stated.

what_this_lane_delivered: the competitor's own hotel inventory for this city is 36, not the 135 its unfiltered page claims
Atlas publishes 99 pet-friendly Cincinnati profiles today, which is 2.75x the competitor's entire city hotel directory, and its census carries 257 identities
the arithmetic proof that this directory mixes vacation rentals into a page labelled hotels
what_this_lane_did_not_deliver: the full 135-row or 36-row served cohort; the listing gates it behind an interactive date selection and this order did not force it
any policy fact whatsoever -- by rule, not by failure
unexplained_gap: not computable from a 12-row sample, and this order does not estimate one. What is bounded is the ceiling: the competitor's whole Cincinnati hotel directory is 36 rows, so no discovery gap larger than 36 can come out of this source for this city.
